subject: language
intro: Mr. Brooks here. Let's plan a vocabulary lesson on using context clues.

beats.narration: Detective framing makes figuring out unknown words feel like solving a mystery.
This standard asks students to use context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
Four named types give students a toolkit.
beats.text: Students will be able to use four types of context clues (definition, synonym, antonym, example) to determine the meaning of unknown words.

beats.narration: Nonsense words prove that context alone can carry meaning.
beats.text: Show a sentence with a nonsense word: "The glorp was so hungry it ate three sandwiches." "What's a glorp? How do you know?"

beats.narration: Signal words make clues easier to spot.
beats.text: Teach each clue type with signal words (such as "or," "like," "unlike," "for example"). Model finding the meaning of real unknown words in a passage.

beats.narration: Checking the dictionary shows how close context can get them.
beats.text: Partners go on a word hunt in a challenging article, recording unknown words, the clue type, their guess, and then checking a dictionary.

beats.narration: This checks both the meaning and the strategy.
beats.text: Read a sentence with an unfamiliar word. What does it mean, and which clue type helped you?

outro: Nonsense words, toolkit, hunt, check. Your turn.
